notes: Distances: 1 unit = 1/256 m (same 3Space v2 scale as ES1; ES2 re-uses several ES1 shapes unchanged, e.g. TOMAHAWK 2030 units tall in both, ES1 HERCULES == ES2 SAMSON geometry). Evidence: the ES2 manual (ENGLISH/ES2GUIDE.HLP) lists Herc heights in metres; posed shape heights (tools/dts_mesh.posed_polys, LOD 0) divided by them give 1/261 m per unit on average (Outlaw 1700u/6.1m, Raptor II 2090/7.0, Tomahawk 2030/7.6, Samson 2364/9.2, Colossus 2460/10.4, Apocalypse 2340/9.5, Ogre 2575/10.4, Diablo 2424/9.0, Hyperion 2363/9.6, Achilles 2263/8.2; spread +-8%), i.e. 1/256 within the precision of the manual. CONFLICT: weapon range texts (LANG0/ENG/WPN_DESC.BIN, 'Autocannon 20 mm. Range: 450 m' ...) match SIMVOL0/DAT/WEAPONS.DAT range fields at exactly 166.7 units per metre (75000/450, 70000/420, 63300/380, 55000/330, 46600/280, ELF 20000/120, EMP 66700/400) - i.e. the designers' weapon ranges read 1.54x longer than the geometric scale. Use metres_per_unit for geometry/positions; if weapon ranges must match the shell text, multiply ranges by 0.006 instead. Speed: unit DAT field 0x04 (speed_forward_max, as ES1) vs the manual's 'Approximate Speed' in KPH gives KPH = 0.306 x field (Outlaw 325 -> 100 KPH, Maverick 285 -> 90, Tomahawk 240 -> 75, Raptor II 215 -> 65, Samson 190 -> 60, Colossus 180 -> 55, Hyperion 140 -> 45, 18 units, spread +-4%), so to_mps = 0.306/3.6 = 0.085 m/s per speed unit. If the field is units per sim tick this implies 0.085/0.00390625 = 21.8 ticks/s (ES1 runtime currently assumes 24); the tick rate itself is not yet verified in DBSIM.EXE (Win32 PE), hence seconds_per_tick null.
